key_insight: A corrected 30-run manikin evidence package successfully preserved complete, video-linked telemetry and provenance fields for a computer-vision airway workflow in structured JSON.
clinical_relevance: This suggests such systems may support later review, auditing, and training by keeping airway video data traceable and organized, without addressing clinical performance here.
method: 30 manikin intubation runs on a HEALTHIBLE simulator with an IntuBlade device and iPhone 15 Pro Max
Six predefined conditions were tested in planned round-robin order, with post-reconciliation review of exported JSON, video manifest, QC fields, and model/app metadata
Blinded video review, independent analysis, and report-quality adjudication were not performed
evidence_signal: After reconciliation, all 30 rows had parseable Study Metrics JSON, matching video/run identifiers, QC pass status, and complete app/model provenance; target rows were 25/25 positive and controls 5/5 negative on the exported target-state flag.
watch_item: This is a manikin-based, post-reconciliation audit of data completeness, so it should not be read as evidence of clinical accuracy, usability, or workflow safety in real patients.
paper_title: Computer-Vision Procedural Telemetry for Airway Guidance: A Public 30-Run Manikin Evidence-Package Audit
